plots.title: Register and view plots
steps: Open My plots and choose to register a plot.
Enter the plot details and draw its boundary on the map.
Save and open the plot details or soil analysis.

campaigns.title: Start a campaign
campaigns.summary: Organize the production cycle of your plot.
steps: Open Campaigns and start one with its plot, crop and sowing date.
Check the details before saving and use the history to follow progress.

expenses.title: Record expenses and review costs
expenses.summary: Track campaign inputs, labor and freight.
steps: Select the relevant plot and campaign.
In My expenses choose inputs, labor or freight and fill in the form.
Save the expense and review the summary and cost reports.

health.title: Review crop health and alerts
health.summary: Review indicators and report field problems.
steps: Select the plot you want to review in Crop health.
Check available indicators and alerts for that plot.
If you find a problem, use Report pest and follow up on the case.

certificates.title: View certificates
steps: Open Certificates and review the available batches.
Select a record to check its information and status.
If a certificate has been issued, use its available link or QR for public verification.

offline.title: Work with an unstable connection
steps: Open the application online and select the plot and campaign.
When recording an expense offline, check that it appears as pending synchronization.
When connection returns, check the synchronization notice and verify there are no remaining pending operations.

connection.question: Can I use the whole application offline?
connection.answer: No. Some field operations, such as recording expenses, support a pending queue. API queries and account updates need a connection. Check the synchronization indicator before closing the application.

contact.question: Does changing my contact email change my login?
contact.answer: No. Your contact email belongs to your profile. To recover access, use the sign-in email shown in your account summary.

alerts.question: Does an alert replace an agronomist assessment?
alerts.answer: Alerts help you decide what to inspect. Read the details, check conditions in the field and seek technical advice when needed.
